meaning: A language model that reads and writes files and runs commands, here used to run a robot policy's improvement loop.
A policy improvement loop in which code resets the scene, runs the policy and scores it, and a coding agent studies the failures, edits the training code and trains again.
A 2026 framework that puts one coding agent on each real robot station to improve the policy against a frozen success check.
One robot with its cameras, one workstation with a GPU and one coding agent; ENPIRE's fleet has eight.
One run of the policy on the robot.
A function that returns pass or fail for one trial; in ENPIRE the agent writes it once with a person and it is then frozen.
The routine that puts the scene back so the next trial can start.
Built once before the loop starts and from then on only read by the agent: the grader, the reset, the safety limits and the evaluation seeds.
Success if the policy completes the task within up to eight sequential attempts inside one rollout; a measure of recovery, different from a one-shot success rate.
The share of research wall-clock time during which the robot is running an experiment.
The share of research wall-clock time during which the station's GPU is in use.
Context a language-model provider has already processed in an earlier call and reads again on the next one.
Training a policy to imitate recorded demonstrations (section 4).
Learning from scored attempts instead of from demonstrations (section 8).
Anything that submits jobs to shared hardware; an agent is one that asks for a GPU in bursts and consumes tokens steadily.
AWS's managed batch scheduler: a job is submitted to a queue and run in a container on instances Batch starts.
The AWS Batch job timeout; a job has none unless this is set.
An AWS feature that runs a pod, task or workload inside its own lightweight virtual machine with its own kernel; it cannot hold a GPU.
A lightweight virtual machine; Nitro Sandboxes use the Firecracker microVM.
AWS's managed Kubernetes.
AWS's own container orchestrator.
